### Custom-field key discovery and audit

Bearer-authenticated `POST /v1/customFields/listKeys` retrieves active custom-field key definitions and can filter by a supplied array of managed entity types. HTTP `200` requires sibling `data` and nullable `next_page`; every result requires `entity`, `key`, and `enforce_uniqueness`, so the operation inventories definitions and their uniqueness setting rather than entity values or mutation outcomes. The body itself is not marked required, `entities` is not required within a supplied object, and unknown-property behavior is unspecified. The response uses the same 19-value `ManagedEntity` enum as key mutations, while the overview names a narrower eight-entity prose set; the sources do not reconcile that applicability boundary or labels such as `product` versus `contract_product`. The page defines no active-state timing, order, total count, page size, cursor lifetime, stable snapshot, concurrent-change behavior, or read-after-mutation visibility. [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]]
warnings: Preserve the definition-inventory scope; do not claim that returned keys have assigned values or that uniqueness currently holds across entity instances.
Do not reconcile the 19-value ManagedEntity schema with the overview's narrower entity prose by inference.
Do not infer omitted-body or unknown-field runtime behavior from the open request schema.

For custom-field configuration audits, bearer-authenticated `POST /v1/customFields/listKeys` returns active key definitions, optionally filtered by managed entity type. HTTP `200` requires sibling `data` and nullable `next_page`, and each item requires entity, key, and uniqueness-setting fields. The endpoint exposes no page-size control, order, total count, cursor lifetime, snapshot consistency, duplicate-or-skip behavior during concurrent key changes, as-of marker, freshness guarantee, or read-after-create/remove visibility. Its inventory also contains no assigned entity values or duplicate-value counts, so it cannot by itself prove value coverage, uniqueness compliance, export completeness, invoice propagation, or external-system reconciliation. [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]]
warnings: Treat the endpoint as configuration discovery, not a complete entity-value or reconciliation report.
Complete cursor traversal does not establish a stable point-in-time inventory while key definitions change.

`POST /v1/customFields/listKeys` is a paginated configuration read under the separate API-wide `Idempotency-Key` authority. After execution admission, identical same-key parameters replay the persisted original result rather than prove a fresh active-key view or new stable pagination snapshot. Advancing query `next_page` or changing the body `entities` filter changes request parameters, so reusing that key then returns HTTP `409` under the API-wide contract. The endpoint does not require the header, prescribe key use across pages, or add local cursor lifetime, cache freshness, concurrent-change, read-after-mutation, another-key, expired-key, or recovery behavior. [[source-metronome-api-reference-custom-fields-list-custom-field-keys]] [[source-metronome-api-reference-idempotency]]
warnings: Keep the execution-admission and changed-parameter behavior sourced to the separate API-wide idempotency authority.
Do not treat replay as a fresh configuration audit or infer a preferred key-per-page policy.
